source.title: Reactivating Alignment: Defending LLMs from Jailbreaks via Intention-Aware Input-Output Matching
source.authors: Luo-Yu Chen; Wei-Qi Wang; Chen-Han Zhang; Zhi-Yi Tian; Shui Yu

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a refusal direction, estimated from harmful-minus-harmless mean activations, as a harmfulness-scoring tool in its SENTINEL defense. It does not test whether that direction causally mediates refusal through ablation or addition, or test the other listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: Section 3.5 describes refusal-direction projection as a scoring component; Appendix F describes RDP as SENTINEL without intention extraction. Figure 2 reports RDP defense comparisons. These results concern projection-based detection, not causal ablation or addition. The paper's SENTINEL results, capability scores, and adaptive-attack results do not test the listed versions. The adaptive attack targets intention extraction, not suppression of the refusal direction.
record.test_reason: The study uses an Arditi-style difference-in-means refusal direction only as a projection-based harmfulness score inside its SENTINEL defense. It never ablates or adds the direction, never edits weights, and never tests jailbreak suppression of the direction. The RDP results report its own defense ablation's detection performance (ASR/FPR), not refusal mediation.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that SENTINEL defends against jailbreaks by extracting intention-revealing input–output subsequences and scoring them with refusal-direction projection. They report lower ASR with limited over-refusal and explain the effect as re-distributing jailbreak features into aligned regions. They make no claim about the direction's causal role in refusal.
record.recipe_differences: The paper estimates normalized harmful-minus-harmless mean activation differences and selects a refusal direction, as in the claim's stated direction-finding recipe. It uses projection scoring at a selected layer and position; it does not ablate or add the direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that RDP score distributions overlap for jailbreak and benign inputs in Figure 2, while SENTINEL's extracted-subsequence scores separate them more clearly. This is sensitivity of the defense's detection performance, not a test of causal direction removal or addition.

fits_no_version.finding: Projecting the full jailbreak context onto the refusal direction (RDP) separates jailbreak from benign inputs poorly on Llama2-7B. Distributions overlap, ASR reaches up to 10% (GCG), and boundary FPR is 35.77%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A refusal-direction projection used as a harmfulness detector on full jailbreak contexts gives overlapping scores for jailbreak and benign inputs.

record.problems: No causal intervention on the refusal direction is performed, so the projection-based results cannot establish that the direction mediates refusal. The RDP values in Figure 2 are reported alongside SENTINEL rather than against a stated no-defense baseline. The study reports no uncertainty estimates for these Figure 2 values.
record.rows_left_out: Left out SENTINEL's own defense results, including its Figure 2 values after the arrows and Tables 1–4, because these assess the proposed intention-extraction defense rather than the refusal direction itself. Left out Table 2 capability results because they measure SENTINEL, not capability after direction ablation. Left out the adaptive-attack metrics in Table 3 because the attack targets intention matching, not refusal-direction suppression.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition of the direction; no refusal-removal, refusal-induction or capability-under-intervention measurements.
Does not test whether jailbreaks suppress the direction. The adaptive attack targets intention matching, and there is no training against ablation.
No multi-direction, affine or cone analysis.
No separation of harm judgment from the refusal decision.
No cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer test. The direction is computed separately per model.
No comparison of training methods or timing.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Figure 4's feature re-distribution argument loosely relates to jailbreaks evading aligned representations, but it measures no suppression of the refusal direction, so it does not bear on V3.

versions.untested_parts: No ablation or addition of a difference-in-means direction; no test of whether refusal is removed or induced; no evaluation of general capability under such intervention.
The adaptive attacker targets SENTINEL's intention matching, not suppression of the refusal direction; no training against direction ablation.
No test of whether refusal uses multiple directions, an affine set, or a cone.
No test separating harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
No transfer test of the direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing.
No test of direction ablation or addition in reasoning models.
